current.text: He is 36 and is coming back from a torn Achilles.
Portland traded for Ja Morant and reportedly plans to start Lillard and Morant together. The projected starting five is Lillard, Morant, Camara, Avdija and Clingan.
Portland's guard group is crowded. Morant and Jrue Holiday were added, Scoot Henderson is back for a full season, and Deni Avdija and Shaedon Sharpe also need the ball.
The crowded guard group lowers his value and adds risk. The guards' combined usage from last season cannot all hold, and minutes and usage should swing from game to game.
Portland is expected to stagger Lillard and Morant but close games with both on the floor.
Portland has a new head coach.
He is expected to play about 30 to 31 minutes as a low-minute starter, with some minutes uncertainty. Josh rejects the view that he is washed or will play only about 25 minutes.
Experts disagree on back-to-backs. One preview does not expect Portland to keep him out of them, while a schedule breakdown sees some worry about back-to-backs early in the season.
Portland has three back-to-backs in the fantasy playoffs.
Three back-to-backs in the fantasy playoffs is not ideal for him.
Experts like his per-game value. Josh sees a possible top 50 player per game, worth about 20 USD on a per-game basis, and another expert expects him to beat his ADP per game.

Experts still pass on him because of his age, the Achilles, possible compensation injuries and missed time. One ranks him Tier 7 among point guards, and in recent mocks experts skipped him even where he was a real option.
Teammates who finish poorly (Camara, Clingan, Avdija) may lower how many of the Portland guards' passes become assists.

durable.text: He is an elite free throw shooter on solid volume and clearly lifts a team's FT%.
His FG% is low for a guard, so a punt FG% team loses little with him.
He is a very good shooter when he plays off the ball.
He carries injury risk: a torn Achilles at an older age, plus concern about compensation injuries.

note: The market prices him cheap: 3.8 USD average cost on Yahoo, 6.2 USD on ESPN, ranks 67 and 70, and he was not drafted in our league last season. Experts value his per-game line at about 20 USD, so in our 144-player auction he is a strong value bid at 5 to 10 USD, mainly for FT%, threes and assists. He fits punt FG% builds best. Early in the season, check whether he really plays 30 or more minutes, how much usage he keeps next to Morant, and whether he plays back-to-backs, because Portland has three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks.
